translations.text: Love wisdom, you rulers of the earth. Consider the power of God with good understanding, and seek him with an open heart.
For he is found by those who do not put him to the test, and he reveals himself to those who do not deny him.
For crooked thinking separates people from God, and power put to the test rebukes fools.
For wisdom does not enter a deceitful soul or dwell in a body enslaved to sin.
For the holy spirit of discipline drives away evil teaching, rises victoriously above the thoughts of fools, and rebukes evil when it comes.

For the spirit of wisdom loves humanity, but will not acquit a blasphemer of what his lips have said. For God witnesses his innermost feelings, is present as an examiner searching his heart, and listens to his tongue.
For the Spirit of God has filled the world, and the one who holds the whole world together has complete knowledge of their words.
Therefore this will not be hidden from him, nor will any spoken word of injustice.

For his judgment will not pass him by when his deeds are exposed. He will question the wicked about the counsel of their thoughts, and the sound of their speech will reach God for the rebuke of their sins.
For it is not without jealous concern that he hears every deed, and the sound of grumbling is not hidden from him.
So guard yourselves against useless grumbling, and restrain your tongues from slander. For a word spoken in secret does not come to nothing, and a mouth that deceives and lies kills the soul.
Restrain your tongues. Do not strive for death through the errors of your life, or bring destruction upon yourselves through the work of your hands.
For God did not make death, and he takes no pleasure in the destruction of the living. For he created creation to exist, and the offspring of the world for preservation.
There is no destructive poison within them to ruin them, and Sheol has no dominion over the earth, for righteousness is immortal.
But the wicked summoned death with their hands and their words. They regarded him as a friend and wasted away for him.
And they made a covenant with him, because they deserved to be his portion.
They said to themselves, without thinking rightly: Our life is short and sorrowful.
There is no cure for a person's death, and no one is known to have returned from Sheol. For we came into being by chance, and afterward we will be as though we had never been created.
For the breath in our nostrils is like smoke, and like the crackle of a spark in the beating of our heart.
When it is extinguished, our body will become dust, and our spirit will disperse like a wisp of cloud. Our name, too, will be forgotten in time, and no one will remember our deeds.
Our life will pass away like the trace of a passing cloud, like mist that disperses, and like fine dew driven away at the feet of [?], vanishing in its heat.
For our life is like a passing shadow, and there is no holding back our death. It is a sealed matter, and no one can reverse it.
Come, then, let us enjoy the good things that are here, and eagerly take pleasure in our life as creatures while we are still in the days of our youth.
Let us fill ourselves with abundant wine and fragrant perfume, and let the season of flowers in the rains not pass us by.
Let us crown ourselves with rose blossoms, arranging them before they wither. And let there be someone who does not share in the flower of our splendor.
Let none of us be excluded from our joy. Everywhere let us leave signs of our folly, for this is our portion and this is our inheritance.
Let us oppress the righteous poor person, and let us not spare [?] or show respect for the gray hair of an elder who has lived many days and years.
Let our strength be our law of righteousness, for weak thinking is said to be worthless.
Come, let us kill the righteous man, for he is troublesome and burdensome to us. He opposes our deeds and reproaches us for sins against the law.
He declares to us the faults of our upbringing and says, 'I have knowledge of God.' He makes himself a son of God and has become a reproach to our thoughts.
Even the sight of him is burdensome to us, because his way of life is unlike that of others, and his path is different.
We are despised in his sight. He keeps away from our paths as though keeping away from something unclean. He declares the final end of the righteous blessed and boasts that God is his father.
Let us see whether his words prove true, and let us test what will come of his vision.
If the righteous man is God's son, God will save him and rescue him from the hands of those who oppose him.
Let us examine him with insult and suffering, so that we may know his gentleness and test his patience.
Let us condemn him to a cruel and disgraceful death, to see whether help will come to him, as he says.
They thought these things and went astray through them, because their wickedness blinded them.
They did not know God's mysteries and did not hope for the reward of righteousness.
They did not recognize the greatness of the honor belonging to pure and blameless souls, for God created humanity without corruption and made it in his own image.
Through the devil's envy, death came and entered the world.
It puts to the test those people who belong to his company.
The souls of the righteous are in God's hand, and torment does not touch them.
In the eyes of fools they seemed to have died, and their [?] was counted as a calamity for them.
Their departure seemed to be destruction, but they are at peace.
Even though they were condemned in the sight of people, their hope with God is perfect life without death.
After being punished a little, they will be worthy of a great reward, because God tested them and found them worthy of him.
He tested them like gold refined in a furnace, and received them favorably, as an acceptable bowl of incense is received.
In the days of their visitation they will shine like the sun and dart about like sparks running through stubble.
They will judge nations and rule peoples, and God will reign over them forever.
Those who trust in him will understand what is right, and his faithful ones will remain with him in love. For grace and honor belong to his chosen ones, and manifest visitation to his righteous ones.
But the ungodly will receive condemnation according to their intentions, and those who have scorned righteousness have gone far from God.
Those who reject wisdom and discipline are fools. Their hope is empty, their suffering and toil are without benefit, and their deeds are useless.
Their wives are foolish, their children rebellious, and their offspring cursed.
For blessed and pure is the barren woman who is blameless and has not known a sinful bed. She will receive fruit at the visitation of souls.
And blessed is the eunuch who has committed no offense with his hands and has thought no evil against God. For he will be given the grace of excellent faith and a desirable share in God's house.
For the fruit of the good person's labor is glorious and beautiful, and the root of his understanding does not perish.
But the children of adulterers will be uprooted, and offspring that come from a bed that transgresses the law will perish.
Even if their stay on earth is long, they will be counted as nothing, and their old age will be dishonorable.
Even if they die quickly, they have no hope and no comfort on the day of judgment.
For the end of an unrighteous generation is evil.
Childlessness with goodness is an excellent thing, for its memory is immortal, because it is known to God.
People honor it while it is present, and when it has passed away, they long for it and love it. In this world it goes about wearing a crown, having won an undefiled contest.
The many offspring of the wicked are of no use. The root of a worthless plant will not become established, nor will it gain a firm footing.
Even if strong foliage appears on its branches for a time, the wind shakes it before it grows tall, and the force of the wind tears it out.
Its branches break before they are fully grown, and their fruit is unripe and worthless, unfit to eat because its season has not come, and useful for nothing.
For children born to wicked people are witnesses to the wickedness of their parents when they are examined.
But when the righteous person's time to die arrives, he will be at rest.
The honor of one's head does not come from many days or from the number of years.
A man's understanding is his gray hair, and a blameless life is a crown for his head.
The one who pleases God is loved. While living among sinners, he departs and is taken away before evil changes his understanding or deceit ensnares his soul.
For zeal for evil darkens good things, and the distraction of desire unsettles the hearts of the innocent.
Even though he died after only a few days, he completed many years, because his soul was pleasing to God.
And [?] he died and departed from among the wicked. But strangers saw this and did not understand it, nor did they take its meaning to heart.
For God's judgment is for his righteous ones, and his visitation will come with mercy upon his chosen ones.
The righteous man, though dead, condemns the wicked while they are still alive; and a young man who dies early condemns the wicked years of the ungodly who acted unjustly.
For they see the death of a wise and righteous person, but they do not understand or know what God planned for him or why God gathered him to himself. They see him and mock him.
But God will laugh at them, and afterward they will suffer a dishonorable fall and become an everlasting disgrace among the dead.
For he will cut them down and uproot them, and they will be found fallen on their faces, speechless.
He will shake them from their roots, and they will remain forever like a wasteland. They will suffer torment, and their memory will perish.
They will come trembling to the accounting for their sins, and their sins will openly accuse them.
Then the righteous person will stand with great boldness before those who afflicted him, denied his labor, and despised his words.
When they see him, they will be shaken with terror and terrible fear, and they will be astonished at his marvelous deliverance.
They will speak among themselves in repentance, grieving and crying out with anguished sighs.
They will say, “This is the one whom we fools once made a laughingstock and a subject of mockery. We considered his life madness and his death dishonorable.
How has he become a son of God, and how has his inheritance come to be among the holy ones?”
We have strayed from the right path. The light of the righteous has not appeared to us, and the sun has not risen upon us.
We filled our paths with sin and destruction, and traveled [?] through the wilderness; we did not know the way of the Lord.
What benefit has pride brought us? What has wealth, together with arrogance, brought us?
All this passes away like a shadow and like a swiftly passing report.
Like a ship that passes through the water and cuts through its waves: after it has passed, no trace of it can be found, and the course of its passage through the waves cannot be known.

Or like a bird flying through the air: no trace of its path can be found. As it passes, its beating wings strike the light air, and it cuts through it with the force of its speed, traveling and rushing onward with the movement of its wings. Afterward, no sign of its passage can be found in the air.
Or like an arrow released into flight: the air is split by it, but immediately comes together again as before, and its passage through it cannot be known.
So we too, as soon as we were born, came to an end. We were unable to show any sign of goodness, but were consumed by our wickedness.

For the hope of the wicked is like a cloud swept away by the wind, like fine [?] driven away by the wind, like smoke dispersed by the wind, and like the memory of a guest who stayed for one day and then departed.
But the righteous and upright will live forever. Their reward is kept with the Lord, and the Most High will care for them.
Therefore they will receive a glorious kingdom and a beautiful crown from the Lord’s hand, because he will shelter them with his right hand and help them with his arm.
He will take up his zeal as his full equipment for war, and he will make his creation a weapon for taking vengeance on his enemies.
He will put on righteousness as a breastplate and crown himself with impartial judgment as a helmet.
He will take up righteousness as an invincible shield.
He will sharpen his wrath into a cutting sword, and the world will take up arms and fight alongside him.
The straight lash of his lightning’s wrath will go against those who stray, to reach them swiftly. But the righteous will be made straight through obedience, like the beautiful curve of the rainbow.
From the rocks of his wrath he will swiftly send down a scourge of hail. The waters of the sea will rage against them, and rivers will surge and swiftly block their way.
A mighty wind will rise against them, winnowing and scattering them like the wind. For sin lays waste the whole earth, and evildoing overturns the thrones of the powerful.
Listen, then, you kings, and understand; learn, you rulers of the ends of the earth.
Pay attention, you who possess vast lands and boast of your many nations.
For the Lord gave you authority, and your power comes from the Most High. He will examine your deeds and test your plans.
Since you are servants of his righteousness, how is it that you do not judge rightly, have not kept his law, and have not walked in the ways of the Lord?
He will swiftly raise up terror against you, for rulers will face severe judgment.
The poor will be pardoned in mercy, but the strong will be subjected to a stern examination.

For the Lord shows no partiality toward anyone and is not overawed by the honor of the great. He made both the great and the small, and he cares alike for everyone, both master and servant, and sets them in order.
But a mighty examination will come upon those in authority.
My words are for you, [?] wicked rulers and oppressors, so that you may learn wisdom and discipline and not fall.
For those who know the commandment of righteousness and keep it faithfully will be justified, and those who learn it will find mercy.
Therefore desire my words, love them, and accept instruction, so that you may find favor and mercy.
Wisdom is very radiant, and her beauty does not fade. Those who love her will see her quickly, and those who seek her will find her.
She reaches those who desire her and makes herself known to them beforehand.
Whoever rises early to seek her will not grow weary, for he will always find her waiting at his door.
For thinking about her is the perfection of understanding, and whoever stays awake for her sake will soon be free from sorrow.
For she herself comes seeking those who are worthy of her. On the paths she shows them her image, in human form [?], and meets them in every thought.
For the beginning of discipline is the desire for her, and taking pains over discipline is love for her.
Love for her is keeping her law, and it is an assurance of incorruptibility.
And incorruptibility brings a person near to God.
Therefore the desire for wisdom leads up to a kingdom.
So if you, rulers of nations, desire thrones and royal authority, honor wisdom so that you may reign forever.
I will tell you what wisdom is and how she came into being, and I will not keep her mysteries hidden from you.
Rather, I will investigate her existence from the beginning and make knowledge of her plain. I will not depart from righteousness or walk in painful envy.
For such a person has no share in wisdom, because a multitude of wise people is the salvation of the world.
A wise king is a support for his people. Therefore accept instruction through my words, and you will benefit.
For I too am a mortal human being, equal to everyone else, a descendant of the earthborn man who was fashioned at the beginning. In my mother's womb I was formed into flesh.
I remained for ten months, taking shape in blood, from a man's seed and the pleasure of sleep in sexual intercourse.
When I was born, I too drew breath like every human being, and I came down onto the earth, which shares my suffering. The first sound I uttered was a cry.
And cries grew loud in sorrow, for no king had a different beginning to his birth.
Everyone has the same entrance into the world, and everyone's departure is alike.
Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given to me. I pleaded, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.
I honored her above royal authority and thrones, and I considered wealth nothing in comparison with her.
I did not compare her with a priceless precious stone, for all gold before her is like a little sand, and silver appears like mud in her presence.
I loved her more than life and physical beauty, and I chose to have her instead of light, because the radiance of the light that comes from within her never fades or sleeps.
All good things came to me together with her, and immeasurable wealth was in her hands.
I rejoiced in them all because wisdom rules over them, though I did not know that she was the maker of all these things.
When I learned this without deceit, I shared her without envy, and I do not hide her riches.
For she is an inexhaustible treasure for humanity. Those who acquired her drew near to God and became his friends through the practice of discipline, which reveals grace.
God also granted me the ability to speak what is pleasing and to think thoughts appropriate to what is given, for he is the guide in wisdom and the director of the wise.
For we are all in his hand, as are our words, all inquiry, and knowledge of crafts.
For he gave me words of truthful knowledge about what exists, so that I might know the ordered structure of the world and the workings of the sun, moon, and stars.
The beginning, end, and middle of times, the turning of days, and the changes of seasons.
And the cycles of the years and the positions of the stars.
And the natures of animals, the spirits of wild beasts, the force of the winds, human thoughts, the varieties of trees, and the active power of roots.
I learned everything hidden and revealed, for the craftsman of every work taught me wisdom.
For in him is a spirit of understanding, holy and only-begotten, which, though one, is divided into many parts.
Subtle [?], swift in its movement, good in its speech, wise, free from defilement, not subject to suffering, ever-present [?], without limit, loving goodness, keen, unstoppable, and beneficent.
Loving humanity, knowledgeable in the art of wisdom, trustworthy, patient, free from anxiety, all-powerful, overseeing everything, and entering into pure, intelligent, and subtle spirits.
For wisdom's movement is swifter than every movement. She extends and moves through everything and passes over everything because of her clear purity.
For she is the flame of God's power and the glory of the Ruler of all, whose form is known, glorious and pure. Therefore nothing unclean comes near her.
For she is the reflection of the ancient light and the untarnished mirror of God's work.
And the image of his goodness. Though she is one, she can do everything; while remaining in herself, she renews everything and passes into the souls of the righteous from generation to generation.
And she makes them friends of God and his prophets, for God loves no one except the person who lives with wisdom.
For she surpasses the sun in beauty and exceeds the whole company of stars.
When compared with light, she is found to rank before it, for night succeeds light, but no evil can overpower wisdom.
She extends powerfully from end to end and orders everything by her goodness. I loved her and sought her from my youth.
I desired to take her as my bride, and I became a lover of her beauty, for her goodness brings one into kinship with God.
And the ruler of everything loved her, for she is wonderful in her knowledge of God's mysteries, and she rises in greatness above all his works.
And where wealth is concerned, she comes before everything for those who possess her in the world.
What surpasses wisdom, the maker of everything? And if knowledge is produced through her,
who among those who exist surpasses her in craftsmanship? And if there is anyone who loves righteousness,
for her labor is good: she teaches purity, wisdom, righteousness, strength, virtues, and good deeds.
And there is nothing in the world more useful or beneficial than she is, nor anything more beneficial for a person's life.
And if anyone loves abundant knowledge and good things, and if he knows what came before and what is to come,
and understands replies in speech and the interpretation of glances, and knows signs and wonders beforehand, and the passing of times and years.
I too decided to take her to live with me, knowing that she would be my counselor in what is good and a comfort that takes away grief and sorrow.
Because of her, I, though young, found praise among the multitude and honor among leaders.
I became eloquent in speech and discerning in judgment, and I was admired in the eyes of the powerful.
When I am silent, they wait for me patiently; when I speak, they listen to me. Even if I speak at length, they put their hands over their mouths.
Through her I found immortality, and they left an everlasting remembrance to those who come after me.
I will govern a people, and nations will be subject to me.
The terrifying rulers of the earth will fear me when they hear of me. In the assembly I will appear kind, and in battle strong.
When I enter my house, I will rest with her, for being with her has no bitterness, no toil or sorrow comes near her, but only joy and gladness.
As I considered this within myself, I sat and rejoiced in her in my heart, knowing that I could not be pure, for kinship with wisdom is immortality.
In loving her there is joy and good gladness; in the work of her hands, inexhaustible wealth; in her speech, instruction in knowledge; and in fellowship with her, words of counsel.
I traveled throughout the whole earth, seeking to take her for myself, so that she might become my bride.
I was a discerning child, and a good soul became mine, for I was good and entered her pure body.
When I knew that I could not be pure unless God gave her to me—
This counsel also came from wisdom: to know whose gift she is. I bowed before God and petitioned him.
And I said with all my heart, “God of my father and Lord of mercy, who made the whole world by your word,
By your wisdom you made humanity to rule over the creation that was made by you,
to exercise dominion on the earth, to govern the world with your goodness and righteousness, and to judge with an upright spirit of judgment.
Give me wisdom, who sits beside your thrones.
Do not reject me from among your servants, for I am your servant, the son of your maidservant, a man weak in strength, short-lived, and lacking in understanding of the law of justice.
Even if someone among humankind is perfect, if the wisdom that comes from you is far from him, he amounts to nothing.
You chose me as king over your people and ruler over your sons and daughters.
You said, ‘Let a house be built on your holy mountain, and an altar in the city of your rest, a likeness of your glorious sanctuary, which you prepared from creation.’
With you is wisdom, who knows your works and was present when you made the world. She understands what is pleasing in your sight and what is right according to your commandments.
send her from the holy heavens so that she may arise and come to me. Send her from the throne of your glory, and let me know what pleases you, so that she may remain with me and labor.
For she knows all your works, which you understand. She will guide me in purity in all my deeds and protect me by her glory, and my deeds will be pleasing.
I will judge your people righteously and be worthy of my ancestors’ thrones.
Who is the person who knows God's counsel? Who can consider and understand what God desires? For the thoughts of mortals are timid, and their thinking is contentious.
For the perishable body covers the soul and weighs it down, and the earthly dwelling covers the mind.

With much strain and anxiety, and with difficulty, if we see, we discover what is done on earth. With toil we discover the work of what we handle with our hands. But who has investigated what is in heaven, and who has known your counsel?
Unless you yourself gave wisdom and sent your Holy Spirit to him from on high.
Through this, the paths of those on earth were made straight, and people learned through wisdom what pleases you and were saved by her.
She guarded the father of the world, who was formed first, when he had been created alone. She sheltered him and saved him from his own transgression.
She gave him strength to rule and hold sway over everything.
And when the unjust and oppressive man departed from her, he perished in wrath, together with the souls of those who murder their brothers.
Likewise, when the earth was flooded, Wisdom saved it and carried the righteous man safely through on a humble wooden vessel.
When the nations came together in a union of evil and distress, she recognized the righteous man and preserved him for God without sin or blemish, and in mercy she preserved a strong son.
She rescued a righteous son from among the wicked who were perishing, and saved him as he fled when fire descended upon the five cities.
To this very day its wilderness remains as a witness, still smoking, and its plants, even when they bear fruit in their season, produce fruit that does not ripen.
And a visible pillar of salt stood as a memorial to a soul that did not believe.

For those who transgressed the commandment not only lacked understanding of the wrath that descended upon them, but also left in the world a memorial of their foolishness, so that they could not hide the sin they had committed.
But Wisdom rescued those who serve her from toil and suffering.

She guided the righteous man who fled from his brother’s anger along a straight path. She showed him the kingdom of God, gave him knowledge of holy things, and increased the wealth he gained from his labor.
And she stood by him against those who cheated and oppressed him.

She helped him, protected him, and sheltered him from his adversaries. She saved him from those who ensnared him and established him when she granted him a mighty struggle, so that he might know that serving God well is stronger than anything.
She did not abandon the righteous man when he was sold, but went down with him into Egypt and saved him from sin.
She did not abandon him in his chains until she brought him royal authority and power over those who had oppressed him.
She exposed the lies of those who had disgraced and rejected him, and gave him everlasting honor.
She rescued a righteous people and a blameless and faultless race from nations that oppressed them, by entering the soul of a servant of God.
She opposed many kings with signs and wonders, and gave the people the reward for their labor.
She guided them wondrously, becoming shade for them by day and light by night in place of the rising stars.
She brought them across a fearsome sea and led them through the midst of mighty waters.
But she drowned their enemies and brought them up from the depths of the sea.
Because of this, the righteous plundered the wicked and praised your holy name, Lord.
Together they praised your hand that fights and conquers, for Wisdom opened the mouths of the mute and made the tongues of infants speak clearly.
For he directed his work through his holy prophet. They journeyed and traveled through a wilderness land where no one lived, and drove in the pegs of their tents in places where no one had traveled.
They confronted those who fought against them and took vengeance on their enemies.
They grew thirsty and called upon you, and water was given to them from a rugged rock.
And relief for their thirst came from hard stone, for by this deed their enemies were judged and killed.
And in this you treated them well when they were distressed and suffering.

Instead of the spring of an unceasing river, which those people had fouled with the blood of the slain, you gave them abundant water, which you caused to gush out swiftly and unexpectedly, as a rebuke to the woman who killed children.
And in the same way you condemned the adversaries when they tested you as they thirsted.
But these were disciplined with mercy and learned how judgment was carried out in wrath.
For you tested these like a father who corrects his children.
But those you pursued and tested like a king without mercy, and in this way you punished them.
You brought them grief both when they were absent and when they were present, for a double sorrow seized them, and the memory of their past experience of evil brought cries of anguish.
When they heard that he had treated them well in their distress, they too regarded it as a blessing from God.
And again, the one whom they had formerly abandoned in misery, they anointed and fled from him in mockery.
And they marveled at the outcome of the issuing of the command. They had not thirsted as the righteous had thirsted.
And in return for the wickedness of their senseless thinking—for when they were misled by it, they worshiped speechless animals, a contemptible and worthless possession—
you sent many speechless animals against them as punishment, so that they would know that people are judged by the very deeds through which they sin.
For your hand, which can do everything, and your right hand, which created the world from formless emptiness, were not unable to send many bears and raging lions against them.
Or else newly created, unknown wild beasts full of fury, breathing fire that blows and blazes; or those that belch out foul-smelling smoke; or those that flash glittering sparks from their eyes.
Not only could their malice and punishment crush them, but even the sight of them would terrify and kill them.
Even without this, they deserved to fall at a single sign, as you pursued them with your word and blew them away with the breath of your power.
Yet you arranged everything by measure, number, and weight, for your great power is always present with you.
Who can withstand the mighty strength of your arm? For the whole world before you is like the tiny tongue of a balance, and like a drop of dew that falls on the earth at dawn.
You have mercy on all, because you have power over all, and you overlook people's sins while you wait for repentance.

You love everything that exists, and you reject nothing that you have made. For you made nothing while hating it; if you had hated anything, you would not have made it. And how could it have endured before you?
And if you yourself had not willed it, how could anything you had not called have been preserved?
You spare and have compassion on all creation.
O Lord, lover of humanity, wisdom is yours, and your good, imperishable spirit is in everything.

Therefore you rebuke those who fall, little by little, with fitting words, reminding them of the sins they have committed and disciplining them, so that, when they examine themselves and turn away from their wickedness, they may believe in you, Lord.
For you hated the former inhabitants of your holy land because of their deeds: their hateful practice of sorcery and their festivals, which were far from righteousness,
their merciless killing of their children, and their communal feasting on people's internal organs, their flesh, and their blood.

For among them the knowledge of the mysteries of your divinity was [?], and they killed a person who had no help from anyone. You wished to destroy their lives by the hands of our ancestors, so that the children of God might receive a dwelling worthy of them, more honored by you than all the earth.
Yet you had mercy even on them, as you have mercy on human beings. When you sent a swarm of hornets ahead, you showed them consideration, so that they would be destroyed little by little.
It was not because you were unable to hand the tyrants over to the righteous, who would capture them in their caves,
or to deliver them to fierce wild animals, or even to destroy them with a single word of your command.
Let this judgment of yours be gradual, as you give them room for repentance. It is not that you do not know that their nature is evil and their wickedness exceedingly great.
And their thinking would never change, because they were an accursed offspring from the beginning. It was not because you feared anyone that you gave them time for the sin they had committed.
Who can say to you, 'What have you done?' Who can oppose your judgment? Who can confront you and call you to account concerning the nations that were destroyed, which you yourself made?

Who is the ruler who will come before you to dispute with you about wicked people? For there is no other God besides you who cares for everyone, so that you should have to show that your judgment was not unjust.
Neither king nor ruler nor prince can contend with you, accusing you concerning those you have condemned.
For you are righteous and order everything righteously. You consider it foreign to your power to condemn someone who does not deserve condemnation.
For your strength is the beginning of righteousness, and your possession and dominion over everything make you merciful toward all.
For you have revealed your strength to anyone who does not believe in the fullness of your power, and you rebuke the arrogance of those who do not believe.
Although you are a mighty judge, you judge with gentleness and care for us with great mercy. Whenever you wish, the power is yours.
Through conduct like this, you taught your people that a righteous person should be kind, compassionate, and loving toward others.
You gave your child good hope, and you told your children that you grant repentance to sinners.
Even though they were enemies of your children and deserved death, you judged them with such great patience and gave them time and a way to escape from evil.
How much more carefully will you judge your children, to whom you gave an oath and a covenant of promise, and, while you discipline, [?] a covenant.
You punish our enemies with many judgments, ten thousandfold, so that when you judge them we may remember your goodness and follow its example.
Even when we are judged, we hope for your mercy. In this way you judged the wicked, who lived their lives lawlessly and persisted in sin.
You judged them through their own impurity, because they had gone far astray along the path of error, calling the most contemptible animals among their enemies gods.
They acted falsely like [?] who had no understanding. Therefore, as upon infants who cannot speak, you sent upon them a punishment resembling their play.
When they were chastised with the chastisement of wrath, they would indeed taste the bread of the righteous Lord’s judgment. For they grumbled at the suffering that overtook them and became angry.

When they were punished through the very things they considered gods, they recognized the one they had previously denied and knew that he was truly God. Therefore the full measure of vengeance overtook them.

For all people who lack knowledge of the living God within them are truly futile. From the beautiful things that are visible, they failed to recognize the one who exists; even while seeing his works, they did not recognize the craftsman.
Instead, they considered fire, swift wind, the circuit of the stars, mighty waters, or the lights of heaven that serve to order the world, and regarded them as gods.
If they made these works into gods because they delighted in the splendor of their appearance, let them know how much better the Lord of these things is, for the author of beauty made this creation.
If they were amazed by their power and activity, let them understand how much more powerful is the one who made them.
They entered into the greatness of creation’s beauty; from the created things they saw, they formed an idea of the Maker of its works.
Yet even so, only a little blame rests on them, because even when they went astray, they were seeking God and wanted to find him. Turning to his works, they searched for him.
They [?] through looking, for the things that appear are beautiful; moreover, their excuse is ample.
For if in this way they could observe so much that they were capable of investigating the world, could they not perceive the Lord of these created things?
But miserable are those whose hope is in dead works, who called the work of human hands gods—things they made from gold and silver with skillful craftsmanship,
or representations of animals, or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand.
Now suppose there is a carpenter who works with wood that is visible and cannot move. He cuts down a well-grown tree and skillfully strips off all its bark.
He skillfully shapes it and makes it into a useful utensil for everyday needs. When he has finished carving, he uses the scraps from his work to prepare food and eats his fill.

Then he takes a piece left over from the wood, useless for anything—a hard, crooked piece covered with knots—and carefully carves it. He shapes it during his leisure time and makes it resemble a human being.
Or he fashioned it to resemble a worthless animal, smeared it with vermilion and painted it, reddened it with [?], and filled in the cracks in it.
He makes a suitable shrine for it, puts it in the place he has prepared for it, fixes it into a recess, and secures it with iron.
He takes care that it does not fall, knowing that it cannot help itself, because it is only an image and needs someone to help it.
Yet he appeals to it about his possessions, his wife, and his children, and he is not ashamed to speak to something that has no life.
He seeks healing from something sick, asks something dead for life, and pleads and prays to something without understanding about his livelihood.

For a journey, he asks something that cannot move or take a single step. For wealth, work, success, and the proper use of his hands and feet, he asks something whose hands can do nothing, seeking from it the gift of strength and speed in his work.
Again, when someone sets out and boards a ship at sea, intending to travel through surging waves, he prays and cries out to a piece of wood more worthless and weaker than the ship carrying him.
For that idol was fashioned out of a desire for profit, and a craftsman made it with skill.
But your guidance, Father, directs everything, for you provided a way through the sea and a secure path through the waves, showing that you can save everything in righteousness.
By bringing him aboard a ship, you have brought even someone without skill safely across, for you do not want the work of your wisdom to remain idle.
Because of this, people entrust their lives to despised and worthless wood, cross through the waves in a small boat or on a raft, and are saved.
Long ago, when the proud giants were destroyed, the hope of the world was carried on wood and kept safe. It survived and left the world the seed of a new generation, preserved by your hand.
For blessed is the wood through which righteousness is accomplished.
But what was made in folly is cursed, as is the one who made it, because it is a perishable work, yet what decays was called a god.
For the wicked person and wickedness alike are hated by God.
For the thing that was made will be condemned along with its maker.
Therefore the idols of the nations will be called to account.

For a created thing became a means of destruction, a snare for human souls, and a trap for the feet of foolish people. For the beginning of sexual immorality was the thought in the mind of the idol’s maker.
Its invention was the corruption of life, for idols did not exist from creation, nor will they exist forever.
Through human folly they entered the world; therefore their end, their passing away and disappearance, will come quickly [?].
Then they conceived the making of an idol: a father suffered and lamented over his only child, because his little one had suddenly been taken away while still [?].
The image they had previously made for a dead man they now honored as a god, and they assigned to it servants of sin, festivals of mourning, and secret sacrifices.

Then, over the course of time, the practice of falsehood and impiety took hold, and they observed it as a law. At the command of wicked rulers, they worshiped carved images. As for those whom people could [?] honor in person,
because they were far away, they reproduced their distant appearance. They made a visible likeness of the king whom they honored, so that the absent one would be as though present.
He pleads with eager insistence. Even those who did not recognize their error persisted in their worship, and they transferred the craftsman’s honor to the work of human hands.
There was also someone who wished to flatter and please the reigning ruler, and he took great care to make his likeness more beautiful and better.
Through this, many people were drawn in because they delighted in the beauty of the work's appearance. The man who formerly received only a little honor they now treated as a god.
This became a trap for the world, because people became enslaved to it through distress or coercion.
They gave the name of God, which cannot be shared, to wood and stone from which they profited.
Moreover, their error in not knowing God was not enough for them. Although they were living amid such a great conflict, in their folly they called such terrible evil peace.
For some kill their children and perform secret mysteries, while others go out singing and shouting according to strange customs unfamiliar to them.
They no longer keep their marriages intact. Instead, one kills another, or else deceives him and raises his hopes with something that will harm him.
All their deeds are mixed with bloodshed, murder, theft, deceit, corruption, ingratitude, faithlessness, and oath-taking.
There is confusion about what is good, forgetfulness of favors, pollution of the soul, alteration of natural birth, disruption of the order of marriage, adultery, and uncleanness.
For the worship of nameless idols is the beginning of every evil and the cause of its culmination. Those who worship them rejoice, go mad, and kill their children.
Or they prophesy and tell lies, or live [?], or swear recklessly.
For they trust in lifeless, false idols and in animals without speech or understanding as though they were the Creator who knows everything. When they swear, they do not expect to be condemned.
Just condemnation overtakes them together, because they thought wrongly about God when they looked to idols, and because they swore unjustly by him with deceit, despising the Creator’s righteousness.
For it is not because of your power, by which they swore, but to pass judgment on their sins, that condemnation continually comes upon the rebellion of the unjust.
But you, our God, are good, gentle, and patient.
In your mercy you order everything. Even if we sin, we are yours, knowing your power. But we will not sin, because we know full well that we belong to you.
For knowing you is perfect righteousness, and knowing your power is the root of immortality.

For neither the wicked, crafty thinking of human beings nor the unprofitable labor of decoration leads us astray, nor handiwork whose colors are changed by painting. The sight of these things draws a fool into desire for them, until he comes to love only a dead image, without a soul or life.
They are lovers of evil, deserving of such a hope—those who make them, those who love them, and those who worship them.
For a potter, too, when he kneads soft clay, makes his various wares, each suitable for the service of each one of us.
From that same clay he makes vessels for use in clean tasks, and for other tasks he makes vessels like them.
The worker in clay is the one who decides and determines the particular use of each of all these vessels.
The one who toils for evil also molds a worthless god from that same clay.
He himself was made from earth only a few days ago, and after a few days he must return to the earth from which he came.
He will be called to account for the judgment of his soul. As for the hardship before him, it is not that he does not know that he must toil and grow weary.
Nor does he consider that his life is short. Instead, he strives to rival silversmiths and goldsmiths and to imitate workers in bronze, and he gives honor to the worthless thing he has made.
His heart is dust, his hope is worth less than earth, and his life is more worthless than clay.
For he does not know the one who made him, breathed into him a soul that gives him power, and breathed into him the spirit of a good life.

Yet they too considered our life a game and a mockery, and our existence a training ground for profit. For he said, “It troubles me that I have sinned,” yet from this he makes a profit and acquires evil.
Indeed, it has become clear that this man sins more than everyone else, because he made an idol, carving it from something found in the earth that quickly decays and perishes.
They are all fools and sorcerers; all the dead among the people, captured and imprisoned in it, exceed even the souls of children in foolishness.

For they regarded the idols of the nations as gods, though these cannot use their eyes to see, their noses to smell the air, their ears to hear, or the fingers of their hands to feel; and their feet are helpless when it comes to walking.
For a human being made them; someone with a spirit allotted to him fashioned them. No human being can make a god like himself.
For although he is mortal, he makes a dead thing with sinful hands. He is better than his gods, because he is alive, but they have no life at all.
They also made animals into gods and worship them in their foolishness. Yet when these are judged with understanding, they are worse than the other gods.
And whoever desired a desire [?], behold, he gained mastery over one of them in the appearance of an animal, and through one he rebelled, because through this God's praise and glory fled.
Therefore they were justly punished, as they deserved, through things resembling their gods, and they were tormented by many harmful creatures that swarm about.
But you treated your people well in the face of their enemies. You gave them quails as food to satisfy their craving, so that they might enjoy the wonderfully flavored food they desired.
But the others, although they desired food, turned away because of the thing sent against them and rejected even what they were accustomed to eating.
These, however, when distress overtook them and they went without food for a few days, were made ready for food of wonderful flavor.
For a summons to punishment called for judgment to come upon those others without delay, because they were violent and wicked, and so that these might see how their enemies alone were tormented.

Even when the fury of fierce beasts came upon them, and they were perishing from the bites of harmful beasts of the earth, your wrath did not persist forever. Rather, they were troubled for a few days so that they might be corrected.
And this sign became a means of salvation for them, reminding them of the commandment of your law.
For whoever among them turned toward it was saved, not by what he saw, but by you, O Savior of all.
Through this you also instructed them and convinced them that you are the one who saves from every evil.
For the bites of locusts and flies killed those others, and no cure was found for their lives, because they deserved to be judged by you in this manner.
But when the venomous fangs of vipers were ordered against your children, your mercy came to them and healed them.

For they experienced this to remind them of your word, and they quickly revived, so that they would not fall into deep forgetfulness, or fall into another way of life and suffering, away from the remembrance of your good deeds.
For it was not the herb they drank or the salve they applied that healed them, but your word, Lord, which heals everything.
For you have authority over death and life. You bring people down to the gates of Sheol and bring them out.
A person kills through wickedness, but once the spirit has departed, he cannot bring it back, nor can the soul that has been taken away be recovered.
But escape from your hand is neither possible nor permitted.
And when you knew that the wicked were denying you, they were punished and destroyed by the strength of your arm.
They were driven by extraordinary rain, hail, and storms from heaven, without mercy or restraint, and they were destroyed by fire.
And the marvelous deed that cannot [?]: fire, which is extinguished by water, became still more active and powerful within it, for the world is a helper of the righteous.
For the flame of the fire became accustomed not to burn the animals that had been sent against the wicked.

Yet when they saw this, they knew that they were being pursued by God's judgment. At times the force of the fire burned still more fiercely in the midst of the water, to ruin and destroy the produce of the unjust land.
Instead, you fed your people the food of angels and sent prepared bread from heaven without their labor, whose taste surpasses everything that tastes good and makes every other flavor seem inferior.

For the image of your form on high revealed the sweetness of your kindness to your children. Its flavor changes for whoever takes some of it, and it serves to fulfill their desires for whatever foods they imagine and wish for.
Hail and snow remained firm alongside fire and did not melt, so that they might know that fire ruined and destroyed their enemies' crops, burning amid the hail and flashing amid the rains.
And again, when the righteous were nourished with this, they forgot the power of their own sustenance, for all creation serves you.
O Creator, you intensify the punishment sent upon the wicked, and you grant comfort to those who trust in you.
And so, at that time, your gift was transformed in every way and served in every kind of food according to the desire of those who asked for it and wanted it.
This was so that your children, whom you loved, Lord, might know that it is not the various crops that nourish human beings, but your word that preserves those who trust in you.
For what fire did not destroy melted when warmed by a little heat from the sun, so that this might be known.
For the sun too hastens to come to us, so that we may praise you and pray to you toward the sunrise.
For the hope of someone who gives no thanks melts like winter frost and flows away like polluted water that is of no use.
For your judgment is great and wondrous beyond telling. Because of this, souls without instruction from the Creator went astray.
For when sinners captured his holy people and overpowered them, the mighty were bound in the darkness of a long night. Then they were fettered beneath the roofs of their houses.
They were found to have strayed from the order of the eternal message, thinking about the sins they had committed against it.
In houses where there was no light, a person would hide in secrecy and be forgotten. They were scattered and wasted away from terror, utterly astonished and troubled by apparitions.
For the [?] that held them could not keep them free from terror, and the sound of a loud voice, whose utterance made them jump, kept troubling them.
The sight of a terrifying apparition destroyed everyone whose face was sorrowful.
The light of fire could not shine even once, nor could the radiance of the bright stars appointed to govern that darkness of night.
But only a sudden fire appeared to them, utterly terrifying. [?] The appearance it showed was worse than the appearances seen when they undertook the foolish labor of sorcery.
The pride of gold and silver was continually mocked by those who scoffed.
For those who hoped to drive away the distress and terror of a sick soul were themselves made sick by a laughable fear, even though nothing disturbing frightened them.
The hissing of flying creatures and of the smallest moving things drove them away and sent them fleeing in terror.
They could not bear to look at the wind rushing from every direction.
For an evil person's unjust deeds bear witness against him and condemn him, and he receives rebuke.
He does terrifying and deceitful deeds, aware of them and examining them in his own understanding.
For the terror of fear is nothing but anticipating thoughts of judgment in one's mind.
And if the hope of the inner mind is small and deficient, it dwells all the more on ignorance and folly, which give way to judgment.
As for those people, when that unbearable night covered them—a night that had truly risen from the depths of the unbearable agony of Sheol—they lay asleep that day.

For terrors frightened them, pursuing them through visions of apparitions and through things that weakened the soul's hope. Suddenly terror and fear overtook them, which they had neither expected nor imagined.
And so it was with everyone there, whoever he might be: whether someone who had fallen or someone held in prison, bound with iron or without iron, whether a farmer or a shepherd.
Indeed, the [?] who labors at the work of the earth dwelt in the wilderness, for he endured the strange misery that befell him, which had no end.
For their whole company was bound with a single chain, the chain of darkness. What overtook them was like this: a whistling wind,
or the pleasant sound of branches in dense, shady trees, or the voices of birds whose song was sweet,
or the sound of rushing water moving with force, or the sound of rocks rolling down terrifyingly.
Or the rush of animals bounding along, whose running could not be seen, or the cries of wild beasts calling out with a frightening voice.
Or the sound of terrifying mountains echoing and passing the sound of birds and wild beasts back and forth among themselves.
Such was the distress that engulfed and terrified them.
For the whole world was shining with radiant light and carrying out its work without hindrance or restraint.
They alone were covered by a heavy night, an image of the darkness that was going to receive them; yet they themselves were a heavier burden to themselves than the darkness.
But among the righteous there was great light, for the others could hear their voices but could not see their appearance.
For they were striking those who loved them, and they were giving thanks because they had caused pain to the oppressed.
But these rejoiced in the gift of deliverance sent to them, and he gave them, as a reward, a shining pillar of fire to guide them along an unknown road.
And a sun that causes distress during the desired sojourn, for those people deserved to be deprived of light.
They were bound in darkness because they had imprisoned and bound your children, to whom the unfading light of the law was being given forever and ever.

When they planned and conspired to kill the children of the righteous, one child was abandoned and survived to their reproach. Through him you destroyed without delay the multitude of their children, and their entire company in abundant water.
Our ancestors knew of that night beforehand, so that, when they knew the oath you had made with them, they would remember it with love.
You received your people [?], salvation for the righteous and destruction for hostile enemies.
For just as you punished those who opposed us, so you honored us when you called us.
For your righteous servants were offering a sacrifice of good cheer, and with one accord they placed the law of your divinity in their hearts.
In this way the holy ones received good things, and suffering also came to those who deserved it.
Our fathers were proclaiming joy as they sang praises, and their voices mingled with the cries and weeping of their enemies, though their words did not harmonize.
Mothers also raised cries of lamentation over their children.
The punishment of slave and master was made equal by the plague.
This affliction overtook the [?] and the king alike, and they all died together in the same way.
Among them were countless bodies of the dead, for the living could not bury the dead, because in a single hour their noble offspring perished and were destroyed.
For because of sorcery she did not believe all the plagues that overtook them; but through the destruction of their firstborn they knew that the people were children of God.
For when stillness and silence, which rules everything, covered all creation, your word—the victor, warrior, and fighter who can do everything—avenged that night.

From heaven, into the midst of the enemies who held royal power, your command came to uproot them from the earth without partiality. Holding a sharp sword, it stood in their midst and filled them all with the affliction of death.
It assailed them from heaven and weighed upon them from the earth. Then it troubled them with the deception of terrifying dreams, and terror they had not expected ruled over them.
Some of them fell in another place, half dead and half alive, and revealed to them the reason why they were dying.
For the dreams that troubled them had told them this beforehand, so that they would not be condemned without knowing why an evil death would overtake and kill them.
Some of the righteous had also previously encountered the anguish of death. There was a downfall in the wilderness, and it brought down many of them.
But the wrath did not last many days, because a blameless man hurried forward and fought, taking up the weapons of his service: the ephod, prayer, and incense.
He found favor when he appeared, opposed the wrath, and brought the plague to an end. By this he showed that he was your messenger, and he overcame the company of destroyers.
It was not by bodily strength or by using weapons of war. Rather, he subdued the one inflicting the plague by your word, reminding him of the ancestors’ oath and their covenant.
For when the dead were falling among them in numbers beyond counting, he stood between the living and the dead, stopped the wrath, and opened a path for the living.
For the entire priesthood of the world was on the hem of his robe, and the glory of the ancestors was on his shoulders, engraved on genuine stones, and your majesty was on the crown upon his head.
The destroyers drew back before this, and these works frightened them, for the plague alone was enough.
But your wrath pressed upon the ungodly until it destroyed them completely, without mercy.
For he knew beforehand what their deeds would be, because they had turned them back from leaving and then sent them away again in great haste.
And when they regretted it, they hurried down and pursued them, saying that snares lay ahead of them.

For while they were still mourning, lamenting and crying out over the graves of their dead, another foolish thought drew them away. They hurried down to pursue as offenders those whom they had begged to leave and had sent away.

The utmost distress they deserved drew them into this deed. Forgetfulness led them astray, and they did not remember what had happened to them, so that they might complete and fill up the punishment still lacking in the number of their punishments.
Your people passed along a wondrous road, but those others met a strange death.
For the whole creation, together with its nature, was fashioned over them anew, still serving the command it had received, so that through it your children might be preserved safely, without harm.
And there was a cloud overshadowing the camp, and where there had previously been water, firm ground and the emergence of dry land appeared.
And an unobstructed road appeared through the Red Sea.
And amid the mighty waves there appeared a growth of green grass, over which all your people passed, sheltered by your glorious hand and your uplifted arm.

When they saw the wondrous work of that hand of yours, they praised it. For they appeared like horses and leaped like calves, praising you, Lord, who had saved them. For they remembered the events of their stay abroad:
how their land brought forth [?] instead of the offspring of animals, and the sea also brought forth many frogs instead of the fish born in the water.
And afterward, when you fed them, they saw a new birth of birds. When they were overcome by craving and asked for rich and pleasant food, many quails came up from the sea to satisfy their craving.
And a punishment came upon the sinners, not far removed from lightning, resembling in its force the miraculous punishments carried out before.
For they were justly condemned, as their wickedness deserved, because they chose to hate foreigners with the worst cruelty. But these welcomed people they did not know when they arrived.
Those others enslaved the people who had stayed among them, even though they had treated them kindly and helped them.
Nor was this all: their deeds would face punishment and investigation, because they treated those who stayed among them harshly.
But these welcomed with feasting those who shared their rights.
And when they afflicted them with great suffering, they were struck with blindness, like those who gathered at the doorway of the righteous. For they were suddenly plunged into thick darkness.
And each of them was searching for the way into the doorway of his own house.

For the lights shifted among them and changed from their own nature. Just as the sound of a song skillfully changes its melody while always remaining in harmony, so too this deed can be fully understood by observing what happened in each thing’s own nature.
For the creatures of the dry land moved into the waters, while those that move about and swim in the water changed their course to the land.
Fire strengthened its power in the waters, and water concealed its natural character.
And the blazing flame, which quickly destroys, moved and spread among them [?].
Nor did they melt the imperishable kind of created substance, the ice-like substance that melts so quickly.
For in every deed, Lord, you increased the glory of your people and glorified them. In everything that came upon us, you did not neglect us or turn away from us, in every place where you are.
